question.problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=-1,$ $x=1,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=1,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F={x}^{2}\,i+xyz\,j+2y\,k,$ the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\,\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y) \\  & =2x+xz+0 \\  & =2x+xz.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}(2x+xz)\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}\,2x+xz\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
